title: Conceptualizing, Measuring, and Managing Customer-Based Brand Equity
author_source: Keller, K. L., Journal of Marketing 57(1), 1-22, 1993, article
note: Defines CBBE as the differential effect of brand knowledge (awareness + image) and specifies associations by type, favourability, strength and uniqueness. This is the conceptual backbone of the brand exploratory: every audit question maps onto one of these dimensions. Also lists direct (experimental, fictitious-brand comparison) and indirect (association elicitation) measurement approaches.
course_use: Core reading, week 1. Students derive their audit questionnaire from the awareness/image taxonomy. Paid (JM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Reflections on customer-based brand equity: perspectives, progress, and priorities
author_source: Keller, K. L., AMS Review 6(1-2), 1-16, 2016, article
note: Keller's own update of CBBE: the brand resonance pyramid, the brand value chain, and the brand audit (inventory + exploratory) placed in a digital, multichannel context. Gives the current 'official' version of the audit process from its originator.
course_use: Reading next to the textbook chapter on brand audits. Can be used to build the audit report structure. Paid (Springer): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Brands and Branding: Research Findings and Future Priorities
author_source: Keller, K. L. & Lehmann, D. R., Marketing Science 25(6), 740-759, 2006, article
note: Review that organises brand research along the brand value chain: company actions, customer mindset, product-market outcomes, financial market outcomes. Useful as a map showing where each audit metric sits, from awareness to price premium to shareholder value.
course_use: Background reading. Use the value-chain figure as the frame for the audit dashboard. Paid (INFORMS): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Branding in a Hyperconnected World: Refocusing Theories and Rethinking Boundaries
author_source: Swaminathan, V., Sorescu, A., Steenkamp, J.-B. E. M., O'Guinn, T. C. G. & Schmitt, B., Journal of Marketing 84(2), 24-46, 2020, article
note: Shows how hyperconnectivity (consumers, brands, devices, platforms) changes brand meaning-making and measurement. Supports adding social listening, platform and algorithmic touchpoints to a classical Keller-style audit.
course_use: Reading for the 'digital brand audit' session. Discussion: which parts of the classic audit are outdated? Paid (JM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Brand audit: Types, Approaches, Methodologies
author_source: Zozul'ov, O., Globa, M., Gnitetskyi, E. et al., Marketing and Digital Technologies 6(2), 86-95, 2022, article
note: One of the few recent articles that classify brand audit types (strategic vs. operational, internal vs. external) and pair them with methods and metric sets. Useful as a checklist-style overview, but it comes from a smaller Ukrainian journal, so students should read it critically.
course_use: Optional reading or source for an audit checklist template. Open access (journal OA policy).

title: A dynamic approach to brand portfolio audit and brand architecture strategy
author_source: Brandão, A., Sousa, J. & Rodrigues, C., European Business Review 32(2), 181-210, 2020, article
note: Proposes a step-by-step brand portfolio audit (role of each brand, overlaps, gaps, architecture fit) and applies it to a company case. One of the few academic sources that operationalise the portfolio/architecture part of an audit.
course_use: Lab: students audit the portfolio of a real company (e.g. Red Bull, Unilever) with the paper's steps. Paid (Emerald): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: The Brand Relationship Spectrum: The Key to the Brand Architecture Challenge
author_source: Aaker, D. A. & Joachimsthaler, E., California Management Review 42(4), 8-23, 2000, article
note: Introduces the brand relationship spectrum (branded house, sub-brands, endorsed brands, house of brands). This is the standard diagnostic grid for the brand-architecture section of a brand inventory.
course_use: Classic reading. Students map a portfolio onto the spectrum as part of the inventory. Paid (CMR/SAGE): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Rethinking brand architecture: a study on industry, company- and product-level drivers of branding strategy
author_source: Strebinger, A., European Journal of Marketing 48(9/10), 1782-1804, 2014, article
note: Empirical study of the industry, company and product factors that drive the choice between corporate and product branding. Gives auditors criteria for judging whether the current architecture fits. The author is at WU Vienna, which makes it useful locally and a possible guest-speaker link.
course_use: Reading for the brand architecture audit session. Paid (EJM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Measuring Brand Equity Across Products and Markets
author_source: Aaker, D. A., California Management Review 38(3), 102-120, 1996, article
note: The 'Brand Equity Ten': ten measures in five groups (loyalty, perceived quality/leadership, associations/differentiation, awareness, market behaviour) with concrete survey questions. Ready-made skeleton for a brand health questionnaire.
course_use: Core reading. Lab: students adapt the Brand Equity Ten into a short survey for a chosen brand. Paid (CMR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Developing and validating a multidimensional consumer-based brand equity scale
author_source: Yoo, B. & Donthu, N., Journal of Business Research 52(1), 1-14, 2001, article
note: The most widely used CBBE scale: brand loyalty, perceived quality, awareness/associations and overall brand equity (OBE), validated across cultures. Short item set that students can use directly in an audit survey.
course_use: Lab instrument: field the Yoo-Donthu items in a class survey and compare brands. Paid (JBR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Developing and validating measures of facets of customer-based brand equity
author_source: Netemeyer, R. G., Krishnan, B., Pullig, C., Wang, G., Yagci, M., Dean, D., Ricks, J. & Wirth, F., Journal of Business Research 57(2), 209-224, 2004, article
note: Scales for perceived quality, perceived value for cost, uniqueness and willingness to pay a price premium, validated across 16 brands in six categories. Links perceptions to price premium, a key audit outcome.
course_use: Lab instrument together with Yoo & Donthu; discuss which facets drive the price premium. Paid (JBR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Measuring customer-based brand equity
author_source: Lassar, W., Mittal, B. & Sharma, A., Journal of Consumer Marketing 12(4), 11-19, 1995, article
note: Early five-dimension CBBE measure (performance, social image, value, trustworthiness, attachment) applied to TVs and watches. A short, intuitive alternative to Yoo & Donthu.
course_use: Comparison reading: students contrast scale dimensions across Aaker, Lassar and Yoo & Donthu. Paid (Emerald): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Consumer-Based Brand Equity Conceptualisation and Measurement: A Literature Review
author_source: Christodoulides, G. & de Chernatony, L., International Journal of Market Research 52(1), 43-66, 2010, article
note: Review that sorts CBBE measurement into direct vs. indirect approaches and compares the main scales and their weaknesses. Good one-stop overview for choosing an instrument for the brand exploratory.
course_use: Background reading before students design their audit survey. Paid (SAGE/IJMR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: The Structure of Survey-Based Brand Metrics
author_source: Lehmann, D. R., Keller, K. L. & Farley, J. U., Journal of International Marketing 16(4), 29-56, 2008, article
note: Factor-analyses 27 common survey brand metrics across categories and countries and reduces them to a small set of underlying dimensions (comprehension, comparative advantage, interpersonal relations, history, preference, attachment). Shows which tracker questions are redundant.
course_use: Use when designing a brand health tracker: which metrics to keep, which to drop. Paid (AMA/SAGE): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: How Well Does Consumer-Based Brand Equity Align with Sales-Based Brand Equity and Marketing-Mix Response?
author_source: Datta, H., Ailawadi, K. L. & van Heerde, H. J., Journal of Marketing 81(3), 1-20, 2017, article
note: Links BAV survey-based brand equity to sales-based brand equity estimated from scanner data (25 categories, 290+ brands). Shows when survey metrics in an audit actually predict market outcomes and marketing-mix elasticities.
course_use: Advanced reading. Discussion: is survey-based audit data 'enough'? Paid (JM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Revenue Premium as an Outcome Measure of Brand Equity
author_source: Ailawadi, K. L., Lehmann, D. R. & Neslin, S. A., Journal of Marketing 67(4), 1-17, 2003, article
note: Proposes revenue premium (brand revenue vs. private label) as a simple, objective product-market measure of brand equity. Gives auditors a market-data metric to complement consumer surveys.
course_use: Calculation exercise: compute the revenue premium from retail data for a category. Paid (JM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: A critical review and reconstruction of perceptual brand equity
author_source: Tasci, A. D. A., International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management 33(1), 166-198, 2021, article
note: Reviews about 200 CBBE studies, finds about 40 component labels and argues for five core components (awareness/familiarity, image, quality, value, loyalty) with a parsimonious measurement framework.
course_use: Background: helps students justify a lean, defensible audit questionnaire. Paid (Emerald): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Brand Concept Maps: A Methodology for Identifying Brand Association Networks
author_source: John, D. R., Loken, B., Kim, K. & Monga, A. B., Journal of Marketing Research 43(4), 549-563, 2006, article
note: Step-by-step BCM procedure (elicitation, mapping, aggregation into a consensus map) demonstrated on the Mayo Clinic brand. A hands-on qualitative-quantitative tool for the brand exploratory.
course_use: Lab: students run a BCM with classmates for one brand and build a consensus map. Paid (JMR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Advanced brand concept maps: A new approach for evaluating the favorability of brand association networks
author_source: Schnittka, O., Sattler, H. & Zenker, S., International Journal of Research in Marketing 29(3), 265-274, 2012, article
note: Extends BCM by adding association favourability and link strength (aBCM), so maps show not only what is associated but whether it helps or hurts the brand. Directly usable as an audit diagnostic.
course_use: Lab follow-up to John et al.: add favourability ratings to the class BCM. Paid (IJRM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Characteristics of memory associations: A consumer-based brand equity perspective
author_source: Krishnan, H. S., International Journal of Research in Marketing 13(4), 389-405, 1996, article
note: Operationalises Keller's association properties through free association: number, valence, uniqueness and origin (direct vs. indirect experience). Shows that high-equity brands differ on these indices, a coding scheme students can reuse.
course_use: Lab: code free-association data with Krishnan's indices. Paid (IJRM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Measuring brand image: a systematic review, practical guidance, and future research directions
author_source: Plumeyer, A., Kottemann, P., Böger, D. & Decker, R., Review of Managerial Science 13(2), 227-265, 2019, article
note: Systematic review of 224 articles covering 12 brand image measurement techniques (scales, free association, BCM, laddering, ZMET, text mining, etc.), with a decision roadmap for choosing a technique. Ideal method-selection guide for the brand exploratory.
course_use: Core reading for method choice. Use the roadmap figure in class. Springer: WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Comparing Methods of Brand Image Measurement
author_source: Driesener, C. & Romaniuk, J., International Journal of Market Research 48(6), 681-698, 2006, article
note: Compares rating scales, ranking and pick-any (free choice) for brand-attribute association and finds that they produce near-identical brand-level results. Supports the cheap pick-any brand-attribute grid as the standard audit format.
course_use: Lab: build a pick-any brand x attribute matrix and a correspondence-analysis map. Paid (SAGE/IJMR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Measuring brand perceptions: Testing quantity and quality
author_source: Romaniuk, J. & Sharp, B., Journal of Targeting, Measurement and Analysis for Marketing 11(3), 218-229, 2003, article
note: Shows that the quantity of brand-attribute responses largely follows brand size (double jeopardy), so raw association scores must be benchmarked against expected values before claiming a brand 'owns' an attribute.
course_use: Important caveat for interpreting audit image grids. Exercise: compute expected vs. observed associations. Paid (Springer/Palgrave): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Seeing the Voice of the Consumer: Metaphor-based Advertising Research
author_source: Zaltman, G. & Coulter, R. H., Journal of Advertising Research 35(4), 35-51, 1995, article
note: Original description of the Zaltman Metaphor Elicitation Technique (ZMET): picture collection, storytelling, construct elicitation, consensus map. The reference method for deep qualitative brand-meaning research in an exploratory.
course_use: Method reading; mini-ZMET interview exercise in pairs. Paid (JAR/T&F): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Laddering Theory, Method, Analysis, and Interpretation
author_source: Reynolds, T. J. & Gutman, J., Journal of Advertising Research 28(1), 11-31, 1988, article
note: Classic how-to for laddering interviews (attribute -> consequence -> value), coding, the implication matrix and the hierarchical value map. Directly applicable for uncovering brand benefits and values in the exploratory.
course_use: Lab: students conduct 3-4 laddering interviews and draw a hierarchical value map. Paid (JAR/T&F): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Dimensions of Brand Personality
author_source: Aaker, J. L., Journal of Marketing Research 34(3), 347-356, 1997, article
note: Develops the 42-item, five-dimension brand personality scale (sincerity, excitement, competence, sophistication, ruggedness). Standard instrument for the personality part of a brand audit.
course_use: Lab instrument: profile 2-3 competing brands on the five dimensions. Paid (JMR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: A new measure of brand personality
author_source: Geuens, M., Weijters, B. & De Wulf, K., International Journal of Research in Marketing 26(2), 97-107, 2009, article
note: Short 12-item, five-factor scale (responsibility, activity, aggressiveness, simplicity, emotionality) that strips non-personality items from Aaker's scale and is validated across brands, categories and countries. A practical replacement for audit surveys.
course_use: Lab: compare Aaker vs. Geuens results for the same brand; discuss validity. Paid (IJRM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Do brand personality scales really measure brand personality?
author_source: Azoulay, A. & Kapferer, J.-N., Journal of Brand Management 11(2), 143-155, 2003, article
note: Kapferer's critique: Aaker's scale mixes personality with other identity facets (e.g. competence, gender). Links to the brand identity prism and supports a critical discussion of audit instruments.
course_use: Debate reading paired with Aaker (1997). Paid (JBM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Mine Your Own Business: Market-Structure Surveillance Through Text Mining
author_source: Netzer, O., Feldman, R., Goldenberg, J. & Fresko, M., Marketing Science 31(3), 521-543, 2012, article
note: Text-mines online forum posts (cars, diabetes drugs) to derive brand co-occurrence networks, perceptual maps and brand-attribute associations, and validates them against survey and sales data. Blueprint for a UGC-based brand exploratory.
course_use: Core reading for the digital audit. Lab: replicate brand co-mention maps from Reddit/reviews in Python/R. Paid (INFORMS): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Mining Brand Perceptions from Twitter Social Networks
author_source: Culotta, A. & Cutler, J., Marketing Science 35(3), 343-362, 2016, article
note: Infers brand perceptions (eco-friendliness, luxury, nutrition) for 200+ brands from the overlap between brand followers and exemplar accounts on Twitter, validated against survey ratings. Scalable, survey-free brand image metric.
course_use: Reading plus discussion of data access after the X/Twitter API changes. Paid (INFORMS): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Mining Marketing Meaning from Online Chatter: Strategic Brand Analysis of Big Data Using Latent Dirichlet Allocation
author_source: Tirunillai, S. & Tellis, G. J., Journal of Marketing Research 51(4), 463-479, 2014, article
note: Uses LDA topic models on about 350,000 reviews across 15 firms and 5 markets to extract quality dimensions, their valence and brand positioning maps over time. Shows how to turn reviews into a dynamic positioning audit.
course_use: Lab: topic-model reviews of competing brands. Paid (JMR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Automated Marketing Research Using Online Customer Reviews
author_source: Lee, T. Y. & Bradlow, E. T., Journal of Marketing Research 48(5), 881-894, 2011, article
note: Extracts product attributes from pros/cons reviews (digital cameras) and builds correspondence-analysis maps that match traditional survey-based perceptual maps.
course_use: Method reading for review-based positioning maps. Paid (JMR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Listen to Your Customers: Insights into Brand Image Using Online Consumer-Generated Product Reviews
author_source: Gensler, S., Völckner, F., Egger, M., Fischbach, K. & Schoder, D., International Journal of Electronic Commerce 20(1), 112-141, 2015, article
note: Text-mining and network approach that derives brand association networks (strength, favourability, uniqueness in Keller's sense) from Amazon reviews and compares them with survey-based BCMs. Bridges classic BCM and UGC mining.
course_use: Reading linking the BCM lab to text mining. Paid (T&F): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Mining the text of online consumer reviews to analyze brand image and brand positioning
author_source: Alzate, M., Arce-Urriza, M. & Cebollada, J., Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services 67, 102989, 2022, article
note: Open-access, step-by-step workflow (text preprocessing, sentiment, association extraction, brand positioning maps) applied to Amazon reviews of competing brands. Easy to replicate as a student project.
course_use: Lab template for a review-based brand exploratory. Open access (CC BY).

title: Visualizing Asymmetric Competition Among More Than 1,000 Products Using Big Search Data
author_source: Ringel, D. M. & Skiera, B., Marketing Science 35(3), 511-534, 2016, article
note: Builds competitive market maps from consumer search/consideration data (price comparison site) for 1,000+ products, including asymmetric competition. Shows how to map the competitive frame of reference for the audit's positioning section.
course_use: Advanced reading. Discussion of the competitive frame of reference. Paid (INFORMS): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: More than a Feeling: Accuracy and Application of Sentiment Analysis
author_source: Hartmann, J., Heitmann, M., Siebert, C. & Schamp, C., International Journal of Research in Marketing 40(1), 75-87, 2023, article
note: Benchmarks dictionary, classic ML and transfer-learning sentiment methods across 272 datasets and shows the accuracy gaps. Essential for judging the quality of social listening/sentiment numbers in a digital brand audit.
course_use: Method reading before students use sentiment tools on brand UGC. Open access (CC BY-NC-ND).

title: A Data Set of Brands and Their Characteristics
author_source: Lovett, M., Peres, R. & Shachar, R., Marketing Science 33(4), 609-617, 2014, article
note: Documents a research dataset on about 700 US brands combining BAV perceptions (differentiation, relevance, esteem, knowledge), personality, word of mouth and advertising. A ready-made data source for brand equity exercises.
course_use: Data lab: students benchmark brands on BAV pillars and relate them to WOM. Paid article; dataset described therein. WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Conceptualizing and measuring brand salience
author_source: Romaniuk, J. & Sharp, B., Marketing Theory 4(4), 327-342, 2004, article
note: Defines brand salience as the propensity to be noticed or come to mind in buying situations and measures it through the breadth of attribute/category-entry-point associations instead of top-of-mind awareness. Foundation of mental availability metrics (MPen, MMS, network size).
course_use: Core reading for the 'Ehrenberg-Bass' view of brand health. Lab: compute mental penetration from a CEP grid. Paid (SAGE): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Building a unique brand identity: measuring the relative ownership potential of brand identity element types
author_source: Ward, E., Yang, S., Romaniuk, J. & Beal, V., Journal of Brand Management 27(4), 393-407, 2020, article
note: Tests 1,281 brand identity elements across 13 CPG categories and 19 countries and proposes 'competitive intensity' as an ownership-potential metric. Characters and logos are easiest to own, colours hardest. Useful for the brand-elements part of the inventory.
course_use: Lab: distinctive-asset audit of a category (who owns which colour/shape?). Paid (JBM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Shape-based assets are strongest: benchmarking distinctive brand asset performance across industries
author_source: Phua, P., Bali, L., Anesbury, Z. & Sharp, B., International Journal of Advertising, 1-23, 2026, article (online first)
note: Benchmarks for Fame and Uniqueness from 1,162 distinctive assets (21 categories, 4 countries, 9 years). Shape-based assets reach about 40% Fame and 71% Uniqueness, colour only about 12% and 39%. Gives students norms to judge their own Fame-Uniqueness grid.
course_use: Lab: run a Fame x Uniqueness distinctive asset survey and compare results with the benchmarks. Open access (CC BY).

title: Assessing branding strength: comparing marketer judgement and consumer data for brand identity elements
author_source: Brus, R., Hartnett, N., Faulkner, M. & Driesener, C., Journal of Brand Management 33(1), 1-17, 2025, article
note: Compares marketers' intuitive judgements with consumer Fame/Uniqueness data for 405 brand elements of 50 brands. Managers overestimate fame and underestimate uniqueness, which makes a strong case for evidence-based asset audits.
course_use: Class experiment: students guess asset strength first, then compare with survey data. Open access (CC BY).

title: How prevalent are suggestive brand names and Distinctive Assets? An AI-human approach
author_source: Bali, L., Anesbury, Z., Phua, P. & Sharp, B., International Journal of Market Research 66(5), 631-649, 2024, article
note: Uses GPT-4 to code about 4,600 brand names and about 600 distinctive assets for suggestiveness, after validating it against human coders. Shows AI-assisted coding for brand inventory work and that suggestive assets score lower on Fame and Uniqueness.
course_use: Example of LLM-assisted inventory coding; students replicate a small coding task. Paid (SAGE): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: The Financial Value Impact of Perceptual Brand Attributes
author_source: Mizik, N. & Jacobson, R., Journal of Marketing Research 45(1), 15-32, 2008, article
note: Links the BAV pillars (differentiation/energy, relevance, esteem, knowledge) to stock returns beyond accounting data. Relevance and energized differentiation carry incremental information for investors. Connects audit metrics to firm value.
course_use: Reading for the 'why audit?' business case session. Paid (JMR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: The Impact of Brand Equity on Customer Acquisition, Retention, and Profit Margin
author_source: Stahl, F., Heitmann, M., Lehmann, D. R. & Neslin, S. A., Journal of Marketing 76(4), 44-63, 2012, article
note: Uses BAV data for US car brands to show which pillars drive acquisition, retention and margin (e.g. knowledge drives acquisition, differentiation drives margin). Translates audit findings into customer-equity consequences.
course_use: Reading; exercise linking audit scores to customer metrics. Paid (JM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: The performance of global brands in the 2008 financial crisis: A test of two brand value measures
author_source: Johansson, J. K., Dimofte, C. V. & Mazvancheryl, S. K., International Journal of Research in Marketing 29(3), 235-245, 2012, article
note: Compares Interbrand financial brand values with consumer-based (EquiTrend) measures in predicting stock performance during the 2008 crisis. Consumer-based measures did better, and the Interbrand values were largely 'blind'. Ideal for critiquing league-table valuations.
course_use: Discussion reading on Interbrand/BrandZ critiques. Paid (IJRM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: A taxonomy of brand valuation practice: Methodologies and purposes
author_source: Salinas, G. & Ambler, T., Journal of Brand Management 17(1), 39-61, 2009, article
note: Classifies brand valuation methods (cost, market, income/royalty relief, Interbrand-type hybrid) by methodology and purpose and shows how much results diverge. Background for the financial-valuation section of an audit and for ISO 10668.
course_use: Background reading; compare Interbrand vs. BrandZ vs. Brand Finance values for one brand. Paid (JBM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Real-Time Brand Reputation Tracking Using Social Media
author_source: Rust, R. T., Rand, W., Huang, M.-H., Stephen, A. T., Brooks, G. & Chabuk, T., Journal of Marketing 85(4), 21-43, 2021, article
note: Builds a weekly brand reputation tracker for top brands from Twitter text, based on the value-brand-relationship drivers of customer equity, and validates it. A model for continuous, social-data-based brand health tracking instead of annual audits.
course_use: Core reading for the brand health tracking session. Paid (JM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Stakeholder Tracking and Analysis: The RepTrak System for Measuring Corporate Reputation
author_source: Fombrun, C. J., Ponzi, L. J. & Newburry, W., Corporate Reputation Review 18(1), 3-24, 2015, article
note: Documents the RepTrak model: an emotional pulse plus seven rational dimensions (products, innovation, workplace, governance, citizenship, leadership, performance), with validation. Standard framework for a corporate reputation audit.
course_use: Lab: rate a company on RepTrak dimensions across stakeholder groups. Paid (Springer/Palgrave): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Managing Brand Experience: The Market Contact Audit
author_source: Chattopadhyay, A. & Laborie, J.-L., Journal of Advertising Research 45(1), 9-16, 2005, article
note: Describes a consumer-based tool for auditing brand contacts (touchpoints): which contacts matter, how strongly they are linked to the brand and their cost-effectiveness. Draws on more than 150 audited brands. Template for the touchpoint audit.
course_use: Lab: students list and score touchpoints for a brand with the contact-audit logic. Paid (JAR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Understanding Customer Experience Throughout the Customer Journey
author_source: Lemon, K. N. & Verhoef, P. C., Journal of Marketing 80(6), 69-96, 2016, article
note: Defines the customer journey (pre-purchase, purchase, post-purchase) and touchpoint types (brand-owned, partner-owned, customer-owned, social/external). Standard framework for structuring the touchpoint part of a brand audit.
course_use: Core reading for the customer experience audit. Paid (JM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Brand Experience: What is It? How is it Measured? Does it Affect Loyalty?
author_source: Brakus, J. J., Schmitt, B. H. & Zarantonello, L., Journal of Marketing 73(3), 52-68, 2009, article
note: 12-item brand experience scale (sensory, affective, intellectual, behavioural), distinct from brand personality and attachment, with effects on satisfaction and loyalty. Ready-made instrument for an experience module in the audit survey.
course_use: Lab instrument. Paid (JM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Towards an identity-based brand equity model
author_source: Burmann, C., Jost-Benz, M. & Riley, N., Journal of Business Research 62(3), 390-397, 2009, article
note: German identity-based branding school (Burmann/Meffert): an integrated brand equity model that combines internal (employee) and external (customer) sources and links behavioural to financial brand equity. Bridges inside-out and outside-in audits.
course_use: Reading for the internal brand audit session. Fits the German-language textbooks (Burmann et al., Identitätsbasierte Markenführung). Paid (JBR): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Employee brand equity: Scale development and validation
author_source: King, C., Grace, D. & Funk, D. C., Journal of Brand Management 19(4), 268-288, 2012, article
note: 11-item, three-factor employee brand equity scale (brand consistent behaviour, brand endorsement, brand allegiance). Directly usable to audit internal branding effectiveness.
course_use: Lab instrument for an internal branding audit (e.g. survey of student employees). Paid (JBM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Employees as influencers: measuring employee brand equity in a social media age
author_source: Smith, D., Jacobson, J. & Rudkowski, J. L., Journal of Product & Brand Management 30(6), 834-853, 2021, article
note: Applies the three EBE dimensions to employees' public Instagram posts (SoulCycle case, 100 images and captions), a qualitative content-analysis approach to auditing internal branding from public data.
course_use: Mini-project: code employee posts of a chosen brand with the EBE scheme. Paid (JPBM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Captivating company: dimensions of attractiveness in employer branding
author_source: Berthon, P., Ewing, M. & Hah, L. L., International Journal of Advertising 24(2), 151-172, 2005, article
note: Develops the 25-item EmpAt scale (interest, social, economic, development, application value). Standard instrument for an employer brand audit, with many later replications (e.g. Viot 2020, JBR).
course_use: Lab instrument for an employer brand audit of a known recruiter. Paid (T&F): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: How strong is the business-to-business brand in the workforce? An empirically-tested model of 'internal brand equity' in a business-to-business setting
author_source: Baumgarth, C. & Schmidt, M., Industrial Marketing Management 39(8), 1250-1260, 2010, article
note: Develops and tests 'internal brand equity' (brand knowledge, commitment, involvement of employees) in German B2B firms and links it to brand-oriented culture and external brand equity. Combines a B2B audit with an internal audit.
course_use: Reading for the B2B/internal audit session. Paid (IMM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: An application of Keller's brand equity model in a B2B context
author_source: Kuhn, K.-A. L., Alpert, F. & Pope, N. K. Ll., Qualitative Market Research 11(1), 40-58, 2008, article
note: Tests the Keller CBBE pyramid qualitatively with B2B buyers (electronic tracking systems) and shows which blocks need adaptation, e.g. corporate brand and sales-staff relationships matter more than product-brand imagery. Guides adapting the audit to B2B.
course_use: Case-like reading for B2B audit projects. Paid (Emerald): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Frontiers: Determining the Validity of Large Language Models for Automated Perceptual Analysis
author_source: Li, P., Castelo, N., Katona, Z. & Sarvary, M., Marketing Science 43(2), 254-266, 2024, article
note: Shows that LLM-generated brand similarity ratings reproduce human-survey perceptual maps with high agreement (above 75%) at a fraction of the cost. Key evidence for AI-based brand perception measurement in audits.
course_use: Lab: students prompt an LLM for brand similarity and attribute ratings, build a perceptual map and compare it with a class survey. Paid (INFORMS): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: AI-Human Hybrids for Marketing Research: Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) as Collaborators
author_source: Arora, N., Chakraborty, I. & Nishimura, Y., Journal of Marketing 89(2), 43-70, 2025, article
note: Evaluates LLMs as synthetic respondents and as co-analysts in qualitative and quantitative research and identifies where they match humans and where they fail. Guidelines for hybrid AI-human brand exploratory research.
course_use: Reading for the AI session. Discussion of the limits of synthetic respondents in audits. Paid (JM): WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Strategic Brand Management: Building, Measuring, and Managing Brand Equity (Global Edition, 5th ed.)
author_source: Kevin Lane Keller & Vanitha Swaminathan, Pearson, 5th ed. (Global Edition), 2020/2023, book
note: Kapitel 9 'Developing a Brand Equity Measurement and Management System' ist die Standardquelle für das Brand Audit: Brand Inventory (Bestandsaufnahme aller Marketingaktivitäten und Markenelemente) + Brand Exploratory (qualitative/quantitative Konsumentenforschung zu Wissen, Assoziationen, Resonanz), dazu Brand Tracking und Brand Equity Charter; Kapitel 10/11 liefern die Messinstrumente (Customer Mind-Set bzw. Marktergebnisse). Der Muster-Brand-Audit im Anhang (frühere Auflagen: Rolex) eignet sich als Strukturvorlage für studentische Audits.
course_use: Kernlektüre + Template für Audit-Projekt; paid (Print ~£81, eText ~£39), ältere Auflagen in WU-Bibliothek prüfen

title: The New Strategic Brand Management: Advanced Insights and Strategic Thinking (5th ed.)
author_source: Jean-Noël Kapferer, Kogan Page, 5th ed., 2012, book
note: Brand Identity Prism (Physique, Personality, Culture, Relationship, Reflection, Self-Image) als Diagnoseraster für den Identitäts-Teil eines Audits (Soll-Identität vs. wahrgenommenes Image); Kapitel zu Brand Equity/Markenbewertung und Markenarchitektur unterstützen die Portfolio-Analyse im Audit.
course_use: Hintergrund/Framework für Identitätsanalyse; paid (~€50), WU-Bibliothek prüfen

title: Managing Brand Equity: Capitalizing on the Value of a Brand Name
author_source: David A. Aaker, Free Press, 1991, book
note: Klassisches Brand-Equity-Modell (Markenloyalität, Bekanntheit, wahrgenommene Qualität, Markenassoziationen, sonstige Assets) – liefert die fünf Dimensionen, nach denen der Consumer-Teil eines Audits gegliedert werden kann.
course_use: Hintergrund/Theorie; paid, WU-Bibliothek prüfen

title: Building Strong Brands
author_source: David A. Aaker, Free Press, 1996, book
note: Brand Identity System (Marke als Produkt, Organisation, Person, Symbol; Kern- vs. erweiterte Identität) und Kapitel 'Measuring Brand Equity Across Products and Markets' (Brand Equity Ten) – direkt als Kennzahlenkatalog für ein Audit nutzbar.
course_use: Reading/Kennzahlenkatalog (Brand Equity Ten); paid, WU-Bibliothek prüfen

title: Aaker on Brands: 20 Principles That Drive Success
author_source: David A. Aaker, Morgan James Publishing, 2014, book
note: Kurze, praxisnahe Prinzipien (Brand Vision, Brand Relevance, Signature Stories, Portfolio) – als Checkliste für die strategische Bewertung im Audit und als leicht lesbare Einstiegslektüre.
course_use: Ergänzende Lektüre/Checkliste; paid (~€20)

title: Strategie und Technik der Markenführung (10. Aufl.)
author_source: Franz-Rudolf Esch & Dennis Esch, Vahlen, 10. Aufl., 2024, book (German)
note: Deutschsprachiges Standardwerk: Markensteuerrad (Kompetenz, Tonalität, Benefit, Markenbild) als Raster für den Soll-Ist-Vergleich der Markenidentität; der Teil zum Markencontrolling (Markenstatus, Markenwert, Imagemessung, Tracking) entspricht inhaltlich einem Markenaudit/Markencheck.
course_use: Kernlektüre (DE) für Markenaudit-Aufbau; paid (~€50), WU-Bibliothek prüfen

title: Identitätsbasierte Markenführung: Grundlagen – Strategie – Umsetzung – Controlling (5. Aufl.)
author_source: Christoph Burmann, Tilo Halaszovich, Michael Schade, Kristina Klein & Rico Piehler, Springer Gabler, 5. Aufl., 2024, book (German)
note: Kapitel zum identitätsbasierten Markencontrolling (Messung der Markenidentität intern vs. Markenimage extern, Brand Commitment, Markenstärke und Markenwert) – liefert das Identitäts-Image-Gap-Modell als Gliederung eines Markenaudits; neue CSR-Sektion (inkl. Greenwashing-Risiken) für Nachhaltigkeits-Audits.
course_use: Kernlektüre (DE); WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink)

title: Identity-Based Brand Management: Fundamentals – Strategy – Implementation – Controlling (3rd ed.)
author_source: Christoph Burmann, Nicola-Maria Riley, Tilo Halaszovich, Michael Schade, Kristina Klein & Rico Piehler, Springer Gabler, 3rd ed., 2025, book
note: Englische Fassung des Bremer Ansatzes; das Controlling-Kapitel (identity-based brand controlling, brand strength, brand value) ist für englischsprachige Kurse die direkte Entsprechung zum Markenaudit.
course_use: Reading (EN); WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink)

title: Marketing: Grundlagen marktorientierter Unternehmensführung (14. Aufl.)
author_source: Heribert Meffert, Christoph Burmann, Manfred Kirchgeorg & Maik Eisenbeiß, Springer Gabler, 14. Aufl., 2024, book (German)
note: Lehrbuch-Klassiker; Teil Marketingcontrolling (inkl. Markencontrolling und Marketing-Audit) sowie Abschnitte zur Markenstrategie – ordnet das Brand Audit in den breiteren Marketing-Audit-/Controlling-Prozess ein.
course_use: Hintergrund (DE); WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Markenpolitik: Markenwirkungen – Markenführung – Markencontrolling – Markenkontext (4. Aufl.)
author_source: Carsten Baumgarth, Springer Gabler, 4. Aufl., 2014, book (German)
note: Eigener Teil Markencontrolling (Markenstärke- und Markenwertmessung, Kennzahlensysteme) vom Autor des 'Marken-Audit'-Ansatzes; methodisch gute Vorlesungsgrundlage für Audit-Instrumente.
course_use: Reading (DE); WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Markenaudit für Kulturinstitutionen: Ganzheitliches Tool zur Analyse und Professionalisierung der Markenführung
author_source: Carsten Baumgarth, Marina Kaluza & Nicole Lohrisch, Springer VS, 2014 (Reihe Kunst- und Kulturmanagement), book (German)
note: Deutschsprachige Monografie, die ein vollständiges Markenaudit-Instrument dokumentiert (Markenmodell, Dimensionen/Indikatoren, Scoring, Audit-Team, Ablauf) – direkt als Template für studentische Audits übertragbar, auch außerhalb des Kultursektors.
course_use: Template/Fallanwendung (DE); WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Handbuch Markenführung
author_source: Franz-Rudolf Esch (Hrsg.), Springer Gabler, 2019 (Springer Reference Wirtschaft), book (German/English chapters)
note: Sammelband u. a. mit dem Beitrag 'Measuring Brand Equity' (Kap. 72) sowie Beiträgen zu Markencontrolling, Image- und Markenwertmessung – einzelne Kapitel als vertiefende Lektüre zu Messansätzen im Audit.
course_use: Vertiefung, kapitelweise; WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Better Brand Health: Measures and Metrics for a How Brands Grow World
author_source: Jenni Romaniuk (with Magda Nenycz-Thiel & Anne Sharp), Oxford University Press (ANZ), 2023, book
note: Evidenzbasierter Gegenentwurf zu klassischen Funnel-Trackern: Mental Availability, Category Entry Points, Mental Market Share, Distinctive Assets; enthält einen Muster-Brand-Health-Tracker und eine Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitung zum eigenen Tracker – ideal für den quantitativen Teil eines Audits.
course_use: Kernlektüre + Template (Tracker); paid (~AUD 60)

title: Building Distinctive Brand Assets
author_source: Jenni Romaniuk, Oxford University Press (ANZ), 2018, book
note: Kapitel 'Measuring asset strength', 'Metrics: Fame', 'Metrics: Uniqueness', 'Metrics: The Grid' – liefern das Distinctive Asset Grid (Fame × Uniqueness) für den Brand-Elements-Teil eines Audits (Logo, Farbe, Figuren, Jingles); mit Studierenden leicht als Mini-Befragung replizierbar.
course_use: Methode/Übung; paid (~AUD 50)

title: How Brands Grow: What Marketers Don't Know
author_source: Byron Sharp, Oxford University Press, 2010, book
note: Empirische Marketinggesetze (Double Jeopardy, Duplication of Purchase, Mental & Physical Availability) – Benchmarks, um Penetrations- und Loyalitätskennzahlen im Audit korrekt zu interpretieren statt Loyalität zu überschätzen.
course_use: Hintergrund/kritische Perspektive; paid (~€35)

title: How Brands Grow Part 2 (Revised Edition): Including Emerging Markets, Services, Durables, B2B and Luxury Brands
author_source: Jenni Romaniuk & Byron Sharp, Oxford University Press, rev. ed., 2021/2022, book
note: Überträgt die Ehrenberg-Bass-Gesetze auf Services, Durables, Luxus und B2B (neues Kapitel 'Getting Down to Business-to-Business Markets') – nützlich, wenn das Audit-Objekt keine FMCG-Marke ist.
course_use: Ergänzung; paid (~€40)

title: Designing Brand Identity: A Comprehensive Guide to the World of Brands and Branding (6th ed.)
author_source: Alina Wheeler & Rob Meyerson, Wiley, 6th ed., 2024, book
note: Process-Teil, Phase 1 'Conducting Research': Marketing Audit, Competitive Audit, Language Audit und Audit-Readout – praxisnahe Checklisten für den visuellen/verbalen Identitäts-Audit (Touchpoint-Inventar); 50+ neue Cases.
course_use: Template/Checklisten für Brand Inventory; paid (~€60)

title: Brand Management: Mastering Research, Theory and Practice (3rd ed.)
author_source: Tilde Heding, Charlotte F. Knudtzen & Mogens Bjerre, Routledge, 3rd ed., 2020, book
note: Acht Brand-Management-Ansätze (ökonomisch, Identität, consumer-based, Persönlichkeit, relational, Community, kulturell, sensorisch) – hilft, die Perspektive eines Audits theoretisch zu begründen und die Methodenwahl (qualitativ vs. quantitativ) zu reflektieren.
course_use: Theoretischer Hintergrund (Master); paid (~£45), WU-Bibliothek prüfen

title: Strategic Brand Management (4th ed.)
author_source: Richard Rosenbaum-Elliott, Larry Percy & Simon Pervan, Oxford University Press, 4th ed., 2018, book
note: Kapitel zu Brand Equity und deren Messung sowie zum Brand Tracking aus kommunikationsorientierter Sicht – Ergänzung zu Keller für die Auswertung von Werbe- und Kommunikationsdaten im Audit.
course_use: Ergänzende Lektüre; paid

title: B2B Brand Management
author_source: Philip Kotler & Waldemar Pfoertsch, Springer, 2006, book
note: Kapitel 'B2B Branding Dimensions', 'Acceleration Through Branding' (B2B-Markenmanagementprozess, Markenmessung) und 'Beware of Branding Pitfalls' – Grundlage für Audits von Industrie-/B2B-Marken.
course_use: Reading für B2B-Fälle; WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Brand Management: A Theoretical and Practical Approach
author_source: Rik Riezebos (with B. Kist & G. Kootstra), FT Prentice Hall, 2003, book
note: Europäisches Lehrbuch mit Kapiteln zu Brand Equity (konsumenten- vs. finanzorientiert) und Markenbewertung – Brücke zwischen Consumer-Audit und monetärer Bewertung.
course_use: Hintergrund; paid/antiquarisch, WU-Bibliothek prüfen

title: Kellogg on Branding in a Hyper-Connected World
author_source: Alice M. Tybout & Tim Calkins (eds.), Wiley, 2019, book
note: Kap. 1 Brand Positioning (Tybout), Kap. 2 Brand Purpose (Stengel et al.), Kap. 3 Brand Portfolio (Calkins), Kapitel zu Customer Experience – Bewertungsraster für Positionierung, Purpose und Portfolio im strategischen Teil eines Audits.
course_use: Ergänzende Lektüre; paid (~€35)

title: From Brand Vision to Brand Evaluation: The Strategic Process of Growing and Strengthening Brands (3rd ed.)
author_source: Leslie de Chernatony, Butterworth-Heinemann/Routledge, 3rd ed., 2010, book
note: Prozessmodell von Brand Vision bis Brand Evaluation; die Schlusskapitel zur Bewertung der Markenperformance (intern/extern, Brand Health) eignen sich als Audit-Ablauf inkl. Mitarbeiter- und Stakeholderperspektive.
course_use: Reading/Prozessmodell; paid, WU-Bibliothek prüfen

title: Brand Management: Brand Strategy, Brand Implementation, and Brand Evaluation
author_source: Oliver Vogler, Springer Gabler, 2026, book
note: Aktuelles Master-Lehrbuch um das Framework 'Brand Management Clock Face' (12 Kapitel); der Teil Brand Evaluation behandelt Markenbewertung und -kontrolle – aktuellste englischsprachige Springer-Quelle zum Thema.
course_use: Reading (Master/Executive); WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Principles of Marketing (OpenStax) – Chapter 9 'Products: Consumer Offerings'
author_source: Maria Gomez Albrecht et al., OpenStax / Rice University, 2023, open textbook
note: Kapitel 9 behandelt Branding (Markenentscheidungen, Brand Equity, Packaging, Produkterlebnis) auf Einführungsniveau – kostenlose Vorbereitungslektüre vor der Audit-Einheit in Bachelor-Kursen.
course_use: Vorbereitende Lektüre; free (CC BY)

title: The Brand Gap (Revised Edition)
author_source: Marty Neumeier, New Riders/Peachpit, rev. ed., 2006, book
note: Kurzes visuelles Buch zur Lücke zwischen Strategie und Kreation (Differentiate, Collaborate, Innovate, Validate, Cultivate) – Disziplin 'Validate' als Einstieg in Audit- und Testlogik; gut für die Kick-off-Diskussion.
course_use: Einstieg/Diskussion; paid (~€25)

title: Brand Failures: The Truth about the 100 Biggest Branding Mistakes of All Time (2nd ed.)
author_source: Matt Haig, Kogan Page, 2nd ed., 2011, book
note: Kurzfälle gescheiterter Extensions, Rebrandings und Kulturmissverständnisse – Materialpool für Übungen 'Was hätte ein Brand Audit früher gezeigt?'.
course_use: Fallmaterial; paid (~€25)

title: Interbrand Best Global Brands 2025 & Brand Valuation Methodology
author_source: Interbrand (Omnicom), 2025, ranking report + methodology PDF 'Brand Valuation: A versatile strategic tool for business'
note: Methodik aus drei Komponenten: Finanzanalyse (Economic Profit), Role of Brand (Anteil der Marke an der Kaufentscheidung) und Brand Strength (interne + externe Faktoren; Aufnahme ab Brand Strength Score 50); das Methodik-PDF erklärt Brand Value Chain und Anwendungen (Tracking, Portfolio, M&A, Lizenzraten). Verknüpft Audit-Ergebnisse mit monetärer Bewertung.
course_use: Reading + Methodenvergleich; free (Ranking & PDF online)

title: Kantar BrandZ Most Valuable Global Brands 2026 – Methodology
author_source: Kantar, 2026, ranking report & methodology page
note: Dreistufig: Financial Value (S&P Capital IQ, Anteil immaterieller Erträge, Brand Multiple) × Brand Contribution (MDS-Modell: Meaningful, Different, Salient → Demand Power, Pricing Power, Future Power) = Brand Value; MDS ist MASB-validiert. Zeigt, wie Konsumentenbefragungen (4,6 Mio. Befragte, 22.000+ Marken) in Markenwert übersetzt werden.
course_use: Reading/Methodenvergleich; free (Report-Download, ggf. Registrierung)

title: Brand Finance Global 500 2026
author_source: Brand Finance, January 2026 (WEF Davos), ranking report
note: Top-500-Markenwerte (gesamt ca. 10,4 Bio. USD, Apple an der Spitze); Brand Strength Index + Royalty Relief; Rankings frei auf Brandirectory – Datengrundlage für Übungen zur Markenwertentwicklung und zum Vergleich mit Interbrand/BrandZ.
course_use: Datenquelle für Übung; free (Ranking), Vollreport teils frei

title: How We Value the Brands in Our Annual Rankings (Brand Finance Methodology)
author_source: Richard Haigh, Brand Finance, 26 Jan 2021, methodology article
note: Schritt-für-Schritt-Erklärung der Royalty-Relief-Methode: BSI (Brand Investment, Brand Equity, Brand Performance; 0–100) → Lizenzratenspanne aus Vergleichsverträgen → markenspezifische Royalty Rate → Umsatzprognose → Barwert; ISO-10668- und IVSC-konform. Ideal für eine Rechenübung im Kurs.
course_use: Template für Bewertungsübung; free

title: Brand Finance Austria 25 (2025; 2026 Update)
author_source: Brand Finance, press releases 3 Sep 2025 / Sep 2026, national ranking report
note: Österreichs 25 wertvollste Marken (2025: 40 Mrd. €, Red Bull 8,7 Mrd. €, Erste stärkste Marke, Billa am schnellsten wachsend; 2026 laut Pressemeldung 46,8 Mrd. €) inkl. BSI und Sustainability Perceptions Value – lokaler Datensatz für WU-Audit-Projekte; Report unter brandirectory.com/reports/austria.
course_use: Datenquelle (AT) für Audit-Projekte; free (Pressemitteilung), Report ggf. Registrierung

title: Österreichische Markenwert-Studie 2026 (23. Ausgabe) & Sustainable Brand Rating Austria
author_source: European Brand Institute (EBI, Wien), 1 July 2026, study/press release
note: Top-10-Markenunternehmen Österreichs (Red Bull ca. 20,1 Mrd. €, Novomatic, Erste Group u. a.; 180 Unternehmen aus 16 Branchen) plus ESG-basiertes Sustainable Brand Rating; Wiener Institut – Gastvortrag möglich. Die Abweichung zu Brand Finance Austria 25 (Red Bull 8,7 vs. ~20 Mrd. €) eignet sich ideal zur Diskussion von Methodenunterschieden.
course_use: Datenquelle (AT) + Methodendiskussion; free (Charts, Pressemitteilung PDF)

title: EBI Methoden zur Markenbewertung / Methods of Brand Evaluation
author_source: European Brand Institute (Wien), methods PDF (DE/EN), undated
note: PDF-Beschreibung der EBI-Bewertungsmethodik (Grundlage der Global-Top-100- und Österreich-Rankings, laut EBI an ISO-Standards orientiert) – deutschsprachige Methodenquelle aus Wien.
course_use: Reading (DE/EN); free

title: ISO 10668:2010 Brand valuation – Requirements for monetary brand valuation
author_source: International Organization for Standardization, 2010, standard
note: Norm zur monetären Markenbewertung: Income-, Market- und Cost-Approach; Anforderungen an rechtliche, verhaltenswissenschaftliche und finanzielle Analyse sowie Reporting – Referenzrahmen, wenn das Audit einen Markenwert ausweist.
course_use: Hintergrund; paid (~CHF 100), Zugang über WU/Austrian Standards prüfen

title: ISO 20671-1:2021 Brand evaluation – Part 1: Principles and fundamentals
author_source: International Organization for Standardization, 2019 (renumbered 2021), standard
note: Erster internationaler Standard zur (nicht-monetären) Markenevaluation: Input-Elemente (tangible, Qualität, Innovation, Service, intangible) und Output-Dimensionen (Recht, Kunde, Markt, Umfeld, Finanzen) mit Beispielindikatoren sowie Prinzipien (Transparenz, Konsistenz, Objektivität) – direkt als Audit-Gliederung nutzbar; ergänzt ISO 10668.
course_use: Framework für Audit-Gliederung; paid (Preview frei bei ANSI Webstore)

title: YouGov Best Global Brands 2025 (BrandIndex methodology)
author_source: YouGov, 2025, white paper
note: BrandIndex-Index aus Impression, Quality, Value, Satisfaction, Reputation, Recommend (28 Märkte, Marken in ≥10 Märkten); dazu 13 Tracking-Metriken (Aided/Ad Awareness, Buzz, WOM, Consideration, Purchase Intent, Current Customer) – Muster für ein Brand-Health-Kennzahlenset im Audit.
course_use: Template für KPI-Set; free (PDF)

title: 2026 Edelman Trust Barometer Special Report: Brands
author_source: Edelman / Edelman Trust Institute, 2026, survey report
note: Brand-Companion zum Trust Barometer (15 Märkte): Vertrauen verengt sich auf Peers, Creators, Earned Media und Algorithmen – Input für die Dimension Markenvertrauen/Reputation im Audit und für die Diskussion der Trust-Messung.
course_use: Reading/Diskussion; free (PDF, ggf. Registrierung)

title: Brand Relevance Index (Prophet)
author_source: Prophet, annual since 2015 (latest 2025), index report
note: Konsumentenbewertung von 300+ Marken in 27 Branchen auf vier Relevanztreibern (customer obsession, pragmatism, innovation, inspiration); Methodik-Seiten früherer Editionen dokumentieren die Markenauswahl – Beispiel für einen Relevanz-Baustein im Audit.
course_use: Beispiel/Benchmark; free

title: World's Simplest Brands (Global Brand Simplicity Index)
author_source: Siegel+Gale, recurring since 2010 (latest editions 2023ff.), index report
note: 15.000+ Befragte in 9 Ländern, 800+ Marken in 25 Branchen nach wahrgenommener Einfachheit bewertet, plus 'Simplicity Dividend' (Mehrzahlungsbereitschaft) – Beispiel für ein erlebnisbezogenes Audit-Kriterium (Customer Experience).
course_use: Beispiel/Benchmark; free

title: Meaningful Brands 2025
author_source: Havas, 2025, global study (incl. Austrian data)
note: Misst persönlichen, funktionalen und kollektiven Nutzen von Marken; Headline: ca. 78 % der Marken könnten verschwinden, ohne vermisst zu werden; Österreich-Auswertung mit 5.724 Interviews zu 159 Marken – AT-Benchmark für Meaningfulness im Audit.
course_use: Benchmark/Diskussion; free (Summary), Vollreport auf Anfrage

title: MASB Brand Investment & Valuation (BIV) Project – Deep Dive
author_source: Marketing Accountability Standards Board (MASB), 2016, presentation/report
note: 18-monatige Tracking-Studie (12 Kategorien, 120 Marken): Brand Preference erklärt ~80 % der Varianz im Mengenmarktanteil (ungestützte Bekanntheit ~48 %); 2015 als BIV-Standard verabschiedet; MASB Marketing Metric Audit Protocol (10 Merkmale idealer Metriken) – Kriterien zur Auswahl valider Audit-KPIs.
course_use: Reading/Metrik-Validierung; free (PDF)

title: Applying the MASB Brand Investment & Valuation Model (White Paper)
author_source: Jim Meier, David Stewart & Frank Findley, MASB, May 2017, white paper
note: Anwendung des BIV-Modells (DCF mit Verknüpfung Brand Preference → Unit Share → Cash Flow) bei MillerCoors – zeigt, wie Audit-Ergebnisse (Präferenz) finanziell übersetzt werden.
course_use: Vertiefung; paid/members only (Summary frei)

title: Marken-Audit: Skizze und Erfahrungen mit einem holistischen Markencontrolling
author_source: Carsten Baumgarth, PraxisWISSEN Marketing 1/2016 (AfM), S. 22–34, DOI 10.15459/95451.2, practitioner paper (German)
note: Kompakte, frei verfügbare Anleitung: Markenmodell mit Dimensionen (Markenorientierung, Markenführung, Branding, markenorientiertes Marketing, verhaltenswiss. Markenstärke, ökonomischer Markenerfolg) und Indikatoren, Scoring/Gewichtung, Audit-Team, drei Phasen (Vorbereitung – Durchführung – Kommunikation); explizit auch als Lehrmethode beschrieben.
course_use: Kernlektüre (DE) + Template für Audit-Projekt; free

title: Markenbewertung: Die DIN ISO-Norm 10668 ('Alles klar?')
author_source: Ottmar Franzen, markenartikel, 09/2011 (via markenlexikon.com), practitioner article (German)
note: Kurze deutschsprachige Einführung in die DIN ISO 10668: Hintergrund der Standardisierung, Anforderungen und Kritik an publizierten Markenwertrankings – Vorbereitung auf die Methodendiskussion Interbrand/BrandZ/Brand Finance/EBI.
course_use: Vorbereitende Lektüre (DE); free

title: Praxis von Markenbewertung und Markenmanagement in deutschen Unternehmen
author_source: Henrik Sattler / PricewaterhouseCoopers, 2006, study (German)
note: Unternehmensbefragung zu Einsatz, Zwecken und Methoden der Markenbewertung – zeigt, wie Markencontrolling/Audits in der Praxis tatsächlich eingesetzt werden.
course_use: Hintergrund (DE); free

title: Monetäre Markenbewertung (BBDO Insights 6)
author_source: Udo Klein-Bölting et al., BBDO Consulting, Sept. 2007, white paper (German)
note: Überblick über monetäre Bewertungsverfahren und die 'Zehn Grundsätze der monetären Markenbewertung' des Brand Valuation Forum (2006) – deutscher Vorläufer von ISO 10668, nützlich als Kriterienkatalog im Audit.
course_use: Hintergrund (DE); free

title: Better Brand Health Tracking (White Paper)
author_source: quantilope (based on Ehrenberg-Bass / Romaniuk framework), white paper
note: Praxisanleitung zum Tracking von Category Entry Points, Mental Availability und Mental Market Share statt klassischer Funnel-Metriken – Fragebogen-Inspiration für den quantitativen Audit-Teil (Anbietermaterial, kritisch lesen).
course_use: Template für Fragebogen; free (Registrierung)

title: NIQ 2026 CMO Outlook
author_source: NielsenIQ (NIQ), 19 Nov 2025, survey report
note: CMO-Befragung: 83 % vertrauen auf Brand Equity, Anteil langfristiger Markenbudgets sinkt auf 55 %, Datenkonnektivität als Barriere – Kontext, warum Brand Audits und Markenmessung in Unternehmen unter Druck stehen.
course_use: Kontext/Diskussion; free (Registrierung)

title: Ipsos Brand Health Tracking / Brand Health Essentials
author_source: Ipsos, 2024–2026, solution pages & insights (e.g. 'Tracking expectations, context and empathy to build successful brands', June 2024)
note: Ipsos-Logik des Brand-Health-Trackings (Top-of-Mind beim Kauf, Erfüllung funktionaler/emotionaler Bedürfnisse, Präferenz ggü. Wettbewerb) – Vergleichsfolie zu Kantar/YouGov für die Kennzahlenwahl im Audit.
course_use: Beispiel Anbieterperspektive; free

title: BAV (Brand Asset Valuator) – Brand Pillars Methodology
author_source: BAV Group (VML/WPP; formerly Young & Rubicam), ongoing global study
note: Vier Säulen Differentiation (Energized Differentiation), Relevance, Esteem, Knowledge; Brand Strength (Differentiation × Relevance) vs. Brand Stature (Esteem × Knowledge) im PowerGrid – klassisches Diagnoseraster für die Positionierungsanalyse im Audit.
course_use: Framework/Übung (PowerGrid); free (Website), Daten paid

title: Brand Audit: 7 Steps to Evaluate Your Brand's Health (With Checklist)
author_source: Brandwatch, brandwatch.com blog, 20 June 2025, guide + checklist
note: 13-minute guide with 7 steps (framework/goals/roles → customer insights → website & SEO analytics → social media & sentiment → brand performance KPIs → competitor benchmarking incl. share of voice and SWOT → action plan & monitoring) plus a 7-area checklist with guiding questions (strategy & identity, messaging & voice, online presence, customer perception, competitive positioning, internal alignment, tools). Vendor content, promotes social listening.
course_use: Pre-reading before the audit project; the 7-area checklist works as an in-class worksheet for student teams. Free.

title: Free Brand Audit Templates (17 templates: worksheet, checklist, report, competitive audit, surveys)
author_source: Joe Weller, Smartsheet, 13 Oct 2021, template collection
note: 17 free templates in Word/PDF/Google Docs/Excel/PowerPoint: brand audit template (core, verbal, visual identity + evaluation), audit report template (executive summary, methodology, results, recommendations, competitive positioning matrix), competitive brand audit (3 competitors side by side), logo/asset audit checklist, brand asset inventory (Excel), employee (internal) and customer (external) feedback surveys, engagement metrics tracker.
course_use: In-class template bank: give teams the report template as the required deliverable format and the internal/external surveys as starting questionnaires. Free download.

title: Branding strategy: Use a three-step brand audit
author_source: Deanna Schmidt, MaRS Discovery District (Toronto), undated, guide + Google Sheets template
note: Simple, teachable 3-step logic: (1) internal audit (team fills form with brand foundations), (2) external audit by an uninvolved outsider who transcribes the website messaging into the same fields (~2 h), then gap comparison, (3) competitive analysis with 2 direct competitors + 1 'stretch comparator'. Linked Google Sheets form with 16 fields (segments, functional/emotional benefits, value proposition, core associations, key messages, proof points, foundation story etc.).
course_use: Ideal for a 90-minute in-class exercise: student pairs act as the 'external auditor' for a real brand's website and compare with the brand's self-description. Free.

title: How To Do a Brand Audit: 8-Step Framework
author_source: Shopify Staff, Shopify blog, 18 Feb 2025, guide
note: 8 steps (checklist → mission review → data collection → external branding consistency → company culture → customer experience → market position → improvements) organised around the three audit areas internal culture / external branding / customer experience. Practitioner/SME perspective, no downloadable template.
course_use: Short pre-reading for undergraduates; contrast with Keller's brand inventory/brand exploratory to show what practitioner guides omit (brand equity measurement). Free.

title: Marken-Audit: Definition, Schritte und wie man ein solches durchführt
author_source: QuestionPro Blog (deutsch), undatiert, Leitfaden
note: German-language 6-step process (Zweck brainstormen → Ziel definieren → Plan mit Aufgaben/Deadlines → Daten erheben inkl. Befragung von Kunden UND Nicht-Kunden → Analyse internes Branding / externes Branding / Customer Experience → Monitoring) with concrete brainstorming questions (Suchergebnisse, Website, Logo, Weiterempfehlung). Vendor blog of a survey tool.
course_use: German pre-reading for Bachelor courses; use the three analysis areas as a structure for the team report. Free.

title: Der komplette Leitfaden zum Thema Markentracking
author_source: Qualtrics (deutsch), 28 Jan 2026, Leitfaden
note: German guide on brand tracking: Markentreue (Kaufabsicht), Markenbekanntheit (gestützt vs. ungestützt, Recall vs. Recognition), Markenassoziationen (offene Textantworten), brand research in practice. No sample questionnaire; vendor perspective (Qualtrics XM).
course_use: Background reading in German before students design a tracking survey; pair with the Attest questionnaire template for concrete items. Free.

title: Free brand tracker survey template (+ example questionnaire)
author_source: Attest, askattest.com, updated 24 June 2026, survey template
note: 16 ready-made tracker questions: category purchase/usage, ranked choice drivers, unprompted and prompted awareness, ever purchased, consideration (next 12 months), brand-attribute statements, last purchase, NPS + reason, channel exposure last month, mirrored questions for a competitor brand. Template runs on the Attest platform (signup), questions readable for free.
course_use: In-class template: students critique and adapt the 16 items (e.g. replace generic attributes with category entry points following Romaniuk) and program them in Qualtrics/LimeSurvey. Article free; platform login.

title: Kantar BrandZ Brand Valuation Methodology
author_source: Kantar, kantar.com, 2026 edition (methodology reviewed annually), methodology page
note: Three-step logic: Financial Value (parent earnings from S&P Capital IQ × intangible ratio × attribution rate × brand multiple) × Brand Contribution (from consumer equity) = Brand Value. Brand equity via Meaningful-Different-Salient framework, yielding Demand Power, Pricing Power and Future Power; 4.6m interviews, 54 markets; MDS validated by MASB.
course_use: Lecture input on combining consumer-based equity with financial valuation; compare with Interbrand and Brand Finance in a 3-column table exercise. Free.

title: Brand Finance methodology for annual brand rankings (Royalty Relief + Brand Strength Index)
author_source: Brand Finance, brandfinance.com, 26 Jan 2021, methodology explainer
note: 7-step Royalty Relief method (BSI 0-100 → sector royalty range → royalty rate, e.g. 0-5% range × BSI 80 = 4% → brand-attributable revenue → forecast → royalty → NPV). BSI pillars Brand Investment / Brand Equity / Brand Performance; references ISO 10668 (brand valuation) and ISO 20671 (brand evaluation).
course_use: Worked numeric example for a calculation exercise; shows how a brand audit's equity scores feed into financial valuation. Free.

title: Interbrand Best Global Brands (2025 ranking, inclusion criteria, methodology PDF)
author_source: Interbrand, interbrand.com, 2025, ranking + methodology
note: Shows the 2025 Top-100 and six inclusion criteria (revenue outside home region, emerging-market presence, public financial data, positive long-term economic profit, global awareness, Brand Strength Score ≥ 50); methodology PDF linked from the page (financial analysis, role of brand, brand strength with ten factors such as clarity, commitment, governance, responsiveness, authenticity, relevance, differentiation, consistency, presence, engagement – factor list taken from Interbrand reports, not shown on the page itself).
course_use: Use the ten brand strength factors as an internal/external audit scorecard for a student team's brand; free (report download may require form).

title: Applying MASB's Model for Brand Valuation
author_source: Marketing Accountability Standards Board (MASB), themasb.org, May 2017, blog post + white paper (Meier, Stewart, Findley)
note: Introduces the Brand Investment & Valuation (BIV) model: behavioural brand preference metric (MSW•ARS choice measure) as core input, linked mathematically to unit share and present value of cash flows; motivated by the Coach–Kate Spade deal. In the BIV study, preference explained ~80% of variance in unit share (89% with price and distribution). Full white paper members-only.
course_use: Advanced Master session on 'which single brand metric matters'; discuss brand preference vs. awareness/attitude batteries. Post free; white paper login.

title: YouGov BrandIndex – US Biggest Brand Movers (definitions of the 13 BrandIndex metrics)
author_source: YouGov, yougov.com, 14 Apr 2023, metrics explainer/ranking
note: Clear one-line definitions of 13 daily-tracked brand health metrics grouped as media (aided awareness, ad awareness, word of mouth, buzz), perception (impression, value, reputation, satisfaction, recommend, quality) and funnel (consideration, purchase intent, current customer); ranking = number of metrics with significant month-on-month increase.
course_use: Reference sheet when students define KPIs for their brand health dashboard; YouGov monthly 'brand movers' articles give free real data for discussion. Free.

title: What Are Category Entry Points? CEP Guide & Examples for Brand Growth
author_source: quantilope, quantilope.com, 25 Feb 2025, guide (vendor)
note: Operationalises Romaniuk's Better Brand Health metrics: Mental Market Share, Mental Penetration, Network Size, Share of Mind, Mental Advantage; CEP generation via 7W framework, ~20 CEPs per tracker; CEP examples for cereals, soft drinks, face wash, fast food, cleaning. Vendor material – metric definitions are useful, product claims less so.
course_use: Handout when students build a CEP-based mental availability module for their audit survey. Free.

title: Markenwert – Definition (Gabler Wirtschaftslexikon)
author_source: Prof. Dr. Christoph Burmann (Universität Bremen), Gabler Wirtschaftslexikon, Lexikoneintrag
note: Short German definition distinguishing the finanzwirtschaftliche Perspektive (sum of future net cash inflows attributable to the brand) from the verhaltenswissenschaftliche Perspektive (more favourable consumer response than to an identical unbranded product); cross-links to Markenimage, Markenbekanntheit, Markenidentität, identitätsbasiertes Markenmanagement. No dedicated Gabler entry 'Markenaudit' found.
course_use: Terminology anchor for German-language courses (WU Bachelor); cite as definition source in student reports. Free.

title: Markenbewertung (Trommsdorff) – Fachtext im Markenlexikon
author_source: Volker Trommsdorff, markenlexikon.com (Textarchiv), Handbuchkapitel als PDF, ~2004, 23 S.
note: 23-page German handbook chapter: brand value as success measure of brand strategy; argues there is no objectively 'true' brand value but standardised, comparable measurement is essential for controlling; overview and critique of valuation approaches (state of 2003: no accepted standards). PDF loads; content summarised from search snippets.
course_use: German background reading for the session on Markenbewertung vs. Markenaudit; good for discussing validity of brand value numbers. Free.

title: Markenwert – zwischen Ratespiel und Standard (Biesalski/Kilian u.a., absatzwirtschaft 11/2015, BDU-Markenbewertung)
author_source: absatzwirtschaft 11/2015, PDF im markenlexikon.com-Archiv, Fachartikel
note: German trade article on monetary brand valuation: rankings with diverging billion-dollar values for the same company make valuation look like a 'Ratespiel'; discusses the BDU principles of brand valuation and standardisation. Large PDF (>10 MB) – fetch aborted, existence confirmed by search.
course_use: Discussion starter: why do Interbrand, BrandZ and Brand Finance disagree? Free.

title: Brand assets: What they are, why they're important, and how to leverage them (incl. Distinctive Asset Grid)
author_source: Canva Learn, canva.com, undated, guide
note: Practical brand asset audit: collect past/current/future elements along the customer journey, gather audience and team feedback (emotions evoked, confusion, correct brand attribution), focus groups; explains the Ehrenberg-Bass Distinctive Asset Grid (Avoid / Use or Lose / Ignore or Test / Invest) with a mascot example. Canva also offers editable 'Brand Audit Presentation' templates (some Pro).
course_use: Hands-on: students audit 5-8 assets of a brand and place them in the grid; Canva templates for the final presentation. Free (Pro templates paid).

title: Brand Health: What Is It and How to Measure It
author_source: Brandwatch, brandwatch.com blog, 15 Nov 2025, guide
note: Metrics (aided/unaided awareness, consideration, perception/attributes, loyalty/advocacy, share of voice, purchase intent) plus 9 steps: link to business objectives, benchmarks (own past, competitors, aspirational), cadence (continuous monitoring, monthly pulse, quarterly deep dive, annual audit), multiple data sources, dashboard design, common mistakes (vanity metrics, method changes). Warns that SOV/sentiment alone lack context.
course_use: Pre-reading for the session linking the one-off audit to continuous tracking; the cadence model is a good slide. Free.

title: Kantar Brand Tracking (solution page)
author_source: Kantar UK, kantar.com, 2026, vendor solution page
note: Shows how a large agency frames modern tracking: always-on 'brand guidance system' integrating survey, search, social and sales data; competitor benchmarking, campaign optimisation, scenario simulation; links to a downloadable brand equity & growth guide and an on-demand webinar (registration).
course_use: Industry-practice illustration (5 min in class) of how agencies sell tracking; contrast with Ritson's annual tracker. Free; extras require registration.

title: The Key Works of Les Binet & Peter Field (IPA resource hub)
author_source: IPA (Institute of Practitioners in Advertising), ipa.co.uk, continuously updated (latest Oct 2025), resource hub
note: Central index of Binet & Field material: The Long and the Short of It (2013), Media in Focus (2017), Effectiveness in Context (2018), 'Share of Search as a predictive measure' (article & webinar, Oct 2020), 'Using Share of Search to gauge consumer demand' (with James Hankins, Nov 2020), 'Share of Search one year on' (2021), Greatest Hits charts. Access per item not stated (some IPA member-only).
course_use: Source list for a session on behavioural brand metrics (share of search as low-cost audit indicator); students compute share of search with Google Trends. Mostly free, some IPA login.

title: Free AI visibility audit with Semrush
author_source: Semrush blog, March 2026, how-to guide (vendor)
note: New audit dimension: does ChatGPT/Gemini/AI Overviews mention and recommend the brand? <30-minute routine with free tools: AI mentions (Domain Overview), AI crawler access (Site Audit 'AI Search Health'), competitor comparison (Free AI Brand Visibility Tool). Vendor content.
course_use: Optional add-on module 'brand audit in the age of AI search'; students run the free checks on their audit brand. Free tools, some features need Semrush account.

title: Marketing-Audit: Die große Aufräum-Checkliste
author_source: HubSpot Blog Deutschland, blog.hubspot.de, Checkliste
note: German HubSpot checklist for the broader marketing audit (Prämissen-Audit, Ziel-/Strategie-Audit, Maßnahmen-Audit, Organisations-Audit). HubSpot has no dedicated, current brand audit article (blog.hubspot.com/marketing/brand-audit returns 404); use this to show where the brand audit sits within the marketing audit.
course_use: Background for positioning the brand audit within marketing controlling; German, free.

title: Brand diagnosis is the brand manager's first job, so prioritise it
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week column, 23 Feb 2023, blog/column
note: Ritson's blueprint for a brand audit: first-year deep diagnosis (secondary data, buyer profiles, ethnography, brand history/founders/archives, large category survey) → annual tracker measuring only the few associations that matter against competitors plus a custom 4-5-stage funnel from qual research; timing of the yearly tracker; derived (not stated) drivers of purchase.
course_use: Core pre-reading; use the 'deep diagnosis vs. annual tracker' distinction to structure the course project. Marketing Week paywall (limited free articles/registration).

title: Mark Ritson: Marketers who skip brand research are doomed to fail
author_source: Michaela Jefferson reporting Mark Ritson, Marketing Week, 23 Mar 2021 (Festival of Marketing), news/blog
note: Argues new CMOs should spend their first ~6 months on diagnosis; two phases: discovery (brand history, secondary data, loyalist research, segment groups) and testing (brand survey, second-stage groups); low-budget route (history, secondary data, ethnography, talking to loyalists); 'no correlation' between research spend and insight quality.
course_use: Short reading to motivate why an audit precedes strategy; good for a debate on qualitative vs. quantitative audit components. Marketing Week login/paywall.

title: Badly designed surveys don't promote sustainability, they harm it
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week column, 1 Nov 2023
note: Dissects survey flaws using a Barclays study (70% say sustainability matters): prompted lists, social desirability, respondent fatigue, consumers' limited self-knowledge; recommends qual first, shorter questionnaires, honesty priming, derived/behavioural data (e.g. conjoint).
course_use: Methods session before students write their audit questionnaire: 'what not to ask'. Marketing Week login/paywall.

title: Mark Ritson: We know what distinctive marketing looks like – now let's agree what to call it
author_source: Mark Ritson, The Drum column, 6 Oct 2025
note: Clarifies terminology for the asset part of an audit (branded recall, brand codes, distinctive brand assets, fluent devices); cites System1×Effies data (emotion, longevity, explicit branding), <50% correct ad attribution, ~7 brand references in a 30-second spot push recall to 100%.
course_use: Reading for the brand identity/asset audit session; students check ads of their audit brand for branding cues. Free.

title: Mark Ritson: Distinctiveness is marketers' main challenge
author_source: Sarah Vizard reporting Mark Ritson, Marketing Week, 10 Oct 2019
note: Distinctiveness/salience ('first they must know it's me') is 70-80% of the job, differentiation overrated – a useful provocation when students decide which audit dimensions to weight.
course_use: Debate prompt (distinctiveness vs. differentiation) in the positioning part of the audit. Marketing Week login/paywall.

title: Marketers' judgement of brand asset strength 'rarely accurate', study finds
author_source: Niamh Carroll, Marketing Week, 23 July 2025 (on Brus, Hartnett, Faulkner & Driesener, Journal of Brand Management)
note: Ehrenberg-Bass study of 400+ brand elements: marketers overestimate fame and underestimate uniqueness of their assets; group judgements more accurate than individual ones; recommends consumer testing with the Distinctive Asset Grid.
course_use: Evidence for why the audit needs external consumer data rather than internal workshops; pair with Canva/EBI grid exercise. Marketing Week login/paywall.

title: What are category entry points? (Mini MBA blog)
author_source: Mark Ritson / Mini MBA team, mba.marketingweek.com, blog post
note: Ritson proposes a tracking funnel starting with category entry points instead of awareness: share of market experiencing each CEP, brand salience per CEP (mental availability), preference, repeat, NPS; criticises 'have you heard of our brand?' as brand-first; suggests tracking both CEP and classic metrics. Domain was unreachable at check time (DNS).
course_use: Short reading to redesign the classic awareness funnel in the student tracker. Free.

title: Brand Audit category (Branding Strategy Insider)
author_source: The Blake Project, Branding Strategy Insider, posts 2007-2012, blog category
note: Five posts: 'The Brand Audit' (2007), 'Brand Audits: Choosing the Auditor' (2007), 'The Brand Audit: Key for Determining Brand Health' (2011), 'Brand Audit: Guardian of Brand Health' (2012), 'Brand Audits: Three Powerful Rings' (2012) – audit of mission/vision, brand essence, promise, personality as perceived by stakeholders, consistency across stakeholder groups, recommendations for equity and positioning.
course_use: Older but concise practitioner framing; assign 'Choosing the Auditor' for a discussion on internal vs. external auditors. Free.

title: Jenni Romaniuk on Better Brand Health (Q&A)
author_source: Jenni Romaniuk interviewed by Contagious, reposted by Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, marketingscience.info, ~2023, interview
note: Principles for brand health tracking from 'Better Brand Health' (OUP 2023): brand health = changes in memory/perceptions within the category; design the tracker for the category (usable by every brand, not one), analyse by buyer/non-buyer rather than demographics, report for the brand.
course_use: Pre-reading before designing the audit survey; check student questionnaires against the three principles. Free.

title: Tuning out the noise to better hear the quiet consumer
author_source: Jenni Romaniuk interviewed by Dave Winterlich (dentsu), Ehrenberg-Bass Institute / Irish Times sponsored, 9 Feb 2024
note: Trackers overweight heavy loyal buyers; separate light and non-buyers; don't assume purchase frequency (window cleaner bought ~once a year); choose loyalty metrics by category (frequency vs. renewal/defection).
course_use: Discussion input on sampling for the audit survey (who to ask). Free.

title: How do you measure 'How Brands Grow'?
author_source: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, marketingscience.info, ~2023 (summary of a Marketing Facts article), blog
note: Short reflection: brand research takes too little account of How Brands Grow; keep existing research but add category entry points and new association/brand strength metrics (Romaniuk). Very brief – use as bridge to the book.
course_use: 5-minute reading to introduce the 'Ehrenberg-Bass vs. traditional tracker' debate. Free.

title: Brands of Distinction
author_source: Jenni Romaniuk, Ehrenberg-Bass Institute (orig. unisabusiness magazine), ~2013, blog
note: Original explanation of the Distinctive Asset Grid: assets must be famous and unique (uniqueness more important); quadrants Use or Lose / Invest / Avoid / Test or Ignore; check what consumers actually store in memory before identity decisions.
course_use: Primary source for the asset-audit exercise. Free.

title: Advertising tracking is broken
author_source: Dr Chris Riquier, Swinburne University (republished from Mumbrella), 17 June 2019
note: Provocative critique: 'the majority of brand measures are meaningless'; perception/consideration charts barely move for established brands; use existing search, social and third-party data first, surveys last; re-allocate tracking budget to media.
course_use: Counter-position for a pro/contra debate on traditional brand trackers. Free.

title: Six things we learnt about 'The Long and the Short of It' – 10 years on
author_source: Carlos Grande, IPA blog, 18 Oct 2023
note: Interview recap with Les Binet and Peter Field: influence of LSOI, short-termism after COVID, announcement of a forthcoming measurement-focused report; context for long-term brand metrics in audits.
course_use: Background reading on why audits must track long-term brand effects, not only activation KPIs. Free.

title: 2022 Prophet Brand Relevance Index
author_source: Scott Davis, Prophet, Feb 2022, insight report/blog
note: Consultancy alternative to equity trackers: 13,500+ US consumers, 293 brands, 27 categories, 16 relevance attributes (pragmatic, customer-obsessed, inspired, innovative); Prophet also offers a self-diagnostic at relevantbrands-2018.prophet.com.
course_use: Students run the free relevance self-diagnostic for their audit brand and critique the attribute list. Free.

title: Zehn Jahre statt 40 Tage: Warum Markenführung mehr Widerstand braucht
